-- UIParent.lua l.14-42: UIPanelWindows["FrameName"] = { area, pushable, whileDead }. Only -- the rows benilla ships today; the ref rows with no benilla window yet (Tabard, -- Battlefield, WorldStateScore, Minigame) join as their windows land (audited -- row-by-row against the bytes, decision 1507). Four have since left that list: the -- doublewide AuctionFrame with decision 1511, PetStableFrame with 1676, HelpFrame with -- 1673, and Petition + GuildRegistrar with 1672 — all of them are rows below. UIPanelWindows = {} UIPanelWindows["GossipFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["MerchantFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The item-text reader (decision 0572, ItemTextFrame.xml): the ref's own l.20 verbatim -- (`UIPanelWindows["ItemTextFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 }`). The missing row -- WAS bug B288 (decision 1507): the reader already opened through ShowUIPanel, but -- unregistered that call is a bare Show() in no slot — so a quest giver's gossip seated -- itself at the left slot straight over the open note, page text and greeting interleaved. -- Registered, the two are ordinary left-slot rivals (both pushable 0): one replaces the -- other, and the replaced reader's own OnHide sends its CloseItemText(). UIPanelWindows["ItemTextFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The mail window (decision 0544): the reference UIParent.lua l.37 registers MailFrame -- area="left", pushable=0. The OpenMailFrame is NOT a panel — it is a UIChildWindow -- (UIParent.lua l.46; 0544 misread that line as UISpecialFrames, 1507 corrects it): shown -- through ShowUIPanel's bare-Show unregistered branch exactly as the ref shows it -- (MailFrame.lua l.206), hidden by SetCenterFrame's child-window loop when a frame takes -- the center seat, and closed with its parent by MailFrame's own OnHide. ESC still closes -- it on our own hard-listed chain in ToggleGameMenu below — never via UISpecialFrames, -- the ADDONS' list (1206), where an addon's `tremove` could break the client's own ESC. UIPanelWindows["MailFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The script error log (decision 1495) — OURS, with no reference row to transcribe. It is -- registered here for exactly one reason: an unregistered frame takes ShowUIPanel's bare -- `frame:Show()` branch (no left-slot placement, and `CloseAllWindows` never sees it), so -- without this row the window would flip IsShown() without landing on screen and ESC would -- not close it. `pushable = 9` puts it behind everything already registered: a diagnostic -- must never shove a player's real window out of the slot it wanted. whileDead is ours by -- the same logic (1507): a Lua error in the death flow is exactly one you need to read. UIPanelWindows["BenillaScriptLogFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 9, whileDead = 1 } -- The trade window (decision 0592 P1, TradeFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.27 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["TradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 }`). Without -- this row ShowUIPanel takes its unregistered branch — a bare frame:Show() with no left-slot -- placement — so the window flips IsShown() but never lands on screen (the bug: OPEN_WINDOW -- arrived on both clients, yet no window). pushable=1 lets a pushable=0 panel (a merchant) -- shove it to center, the reference's browse-while-trading arbitration. UIPanelWindows["TradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 } -- The trainer window (decision 0237 phase 3, TrainerFrame.xml): an NPC session exactly like -- Gossip/Merchant above (area "left", pushable 0) — competes for/replaces them at the slot. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTrainerFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The bank window (decision 0604 phase 4, BankFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.28 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["BankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 }`), quoted -- verbatim — the same left-slot competition as the other NPC-session windows above. UIPanelWindows["BankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 } -- The taxi-map window (decision 0484 phase 2, TaxiFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua -- registration line (`UIPanelWindows["TaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 }`), -- quoted verbatim — same left-slot competition as Gossip/Merchant/Trainer above. UIPanelWindows["TaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The stable-master window (decision 1676, PetStable.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.39 -- registration line (`UIPanelWindows["PetStableFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 }`), -- quoted verbatim — the same left-slot competition as Gossip/Merchant/Trainer/Taxi above, -- which is what makes the stable master's gossip window give way to the stable it opens. -- The reference lists it between MailFrame (l.37) and DressUpFrame (l.41), which is where -- it sits here too, inside the NPC-session cluster those rows are grouped into. UIPanelWindows["PetStableFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The auction house (decision 1511, AuctionFrame.xml): the reference's own registration, -- quoted verbatim from `Blizzard_AuctionUI.lua` l.13 rather than UIParent.lua — the window -- ships as a loadable addon there, so it registers its own row. **The one and only -- `doublewide` row in all of 1.12**: an 832-wide window takes the left AND centre seats at -- once, which is why the slice above exists at all. Its `pushable = 0` is quoted and inert -- — ShowUIPanel's doublewide arm never consults it (l.392-397). UIPanelWindows["AuctionFrame"] = { area = "doublewide", pushable = 0 } -- The dressing room (decision 1060, DressUpFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.41 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["DressUpFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 2 }`), quoted -- verbatim — pushable=2 lets the NPC-session windows (pushable=0) shove it aside, which is -- what makes "ctrl-click a merchant's item" show both. UIPanelWindows["DressUpFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 2 } UIPanelWindows["QuestFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The ref's own l.25 verbatim — whileDead carried since 1507: `UnitIsDead` is a live unit -- binding now, so the flag decides, and checking your quest log while dead is 1.12's call. UIPanelWindows["QuestLogFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } UIPanelWindows["LootFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 7 } -- The character window (decision 0208 phase 1a, CharacterFrame.xml): the ref's own row is -- `{ area = "left", pushable = 2 , whileDead = 1}` (UIParent.lua l.19, spacing and all) — -- NOT the pushable=0 this line carried from 0208 until 1507 re-read the bytes. The 2 is -- load-bearing arbitration: an NPC session (pushable 0) opening under an open character -- sheet slides it to the center seat — vendor left, your equipment beside it — instead of -- replacing it; and whileDead=1 lets you look your corpse's gear over while dead. UIPanelWindows["CharacterFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 2, whileDead = 1 } -- The inspect window (decision 0631, InspectFrame.xml): the ref's own InspectFrame row -- (`Blizzard_InspectUI.lua:4` — area "left", pushable 0), so inspecting swaps out whichever -- left-slot window was open, exactly as the character window does. UIPanelWindows["InspectFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The spellbook (decision 0216 §8, SpellBookFrame.xml): the ref's own SpellBookFrame row -- verbatim (`{ area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 }`, UIParent.lua l.21; whileDead -- carried since 1507) — same left-slot competition as every window above. UIPanelWindows["SpellBookFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The talent window (decision 0304 §4, TalentFrame.xml): the ref's own TalentFrame row -- verbatim (`{ area = "left", pushable = 6, whileDead = 1 }`, Blizzard_TalentUI.lua:71) — -- pushable 6 one tier above the plain NPC-session/player-state windows' 0. whileDead was -- omitted here while `UnitIsDead` didn't exist; it is a live unit binding now, so 1507 -- carries the ref's flag on every row that has one. UIPanelWindows["TalentFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6, whileDead = 1 } -- The social window (decision 0668) — the ref's own registration line verbatim -- (`UIPanelWindows["FriendsFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 }`, -- UIParent.lua l.29). whileDead: a corpse run is exactly when you want to whisper someone. UIPanelWindows["FriendsFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The two guild-charter windows (decision 1672), the ref's own UIParent.lua l.33-34 -- verbatim. They are ordinary left-slot rivals of each other and of the gossip menu, all -- pushable 0 — which is exactly right: selecting the registrar's gossip row makes the -- server close the menu and push the charter list, so the registrar replacing the gossip -- window in the same slot IS the handoff. Both must be registered or ShowUIPanel degrades -- to a bare Show() in no slot, which is what left the item-text reader interleaved with a -- gossip window in B288 (1507). UIPanelWindows["GuildRegistrarFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["PetitionFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The macro window (decision 0983, MacroFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration line -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["MacroFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 5, whileDead = 1 }`, -- Blizzard_MacroUI.lua:7). whileDead is the ref's and it earns its keep: writing a macro -- during a corpse run is a real thing people do. UIPanelWindows["MacroFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 5, whileDead = 1 } -- The crafting window (decision 0437 phase 2, TradeSkillFrame.xml): NOT an NPC session (it -- opens off your own cast, TradeSkillFrame.xml's own header comment) — the ref Lua's own -- registration line (Blizzard_TradeSkillUI.lua:13) is `{ area = "left", pushable = 3 }`, -- quoted verbatim. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTradeSkillFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 3 } -- The Enchanting window (decision 0437 phase 3, CraftFrame.xml): the ref Lua's own -- registration line (`Blizzard_CraftUI.lua:24`), quoted verbatim — `pushable = 4`, NOT `3` -- (grepped both ref files directly to confirm: `3` is TradeSkillFrame's own line-13 value, -- a different window/depth — CraftFrame.xml's own header comment has the same note). UIPanelWindows["BenillaCraftFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 4 } -- The game menu (decision 0674, GameMenuFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration line -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["GameMenuFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, -- whileDead = 1 }`, UIParent.lua l.15), and the FIRST **center**-area row benilla ships. -- "center" is not a position here, it is a MODE: a native-center frame takes the center -- slot keeping its own anchor (the menu is screen-CENTER by its own XML), closes every -- other window on the way in, and — while it holds the slot — makes ShowUIPanel refuse -- every non-center panel (`CanOpenPanels` below). That is the rule behind "you can't open -- anything with the ESC menu up". whileDead: dying is exactly when you want to log out. UIPanelWindows["GameMenuFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The options window (decision 0950, OptionsFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["OptionsFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, -- whileDead = 1 }`, UIParent.lua l.16): the second native-center row. Same MODE as the -- menu above — it takes the screen, and dying is exactly when you might want to retune -- the client. (The ref's l.17-18 register SoundOptionsFrame/UIOptionsFrame the same way; -- those panels are this one window's category rows now, so the rows have no frames.) UIPanelWindows["OptionsFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The GM help window (HelpFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration verbatim -- (`UIPanelWindows["HelpFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 }`, -- UIParent.lua l.35): the THIRD native-center row, and the first one that is not part of -- the settings shell. Same MODE as the two above — it keeps its own screen-CENTER anchor, -- closes every other window on the way in, and while it holds the slot ShowUIPanel refuses -- every non-center panel (`CanOpenPanels` below). That is deliberate here rather than -- incidental: petitioning a GM is a full stop, not something you do beside your bags. -- whileDead, because being dead somewhere you cannot leave is one of the things you page a -- GM about — and it is what lets the ticket toast's HELP_TICKET dialog reach the window -- from a corpse. (The ref's l.40 WorldStateScoreFrame row is center too; no frame here.) UIPanelWindows["HelpFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- (0997's KeyBindingFrame row is gone — decision 1008 folded key bindings into the -- options window above, the 1.15 layout's own placement; KeyBindingsPage.xml.) -- The world map (decision 0203 phase 2) — the ref's own line verbatim (UIParent.lua l.30) -- and the first **full** row. It was a plain toplevel until now, showing itself with a bare -- `WorldMapFrame:Show()` and so bypassing this manager entirely: with the game menu up it -- was the ONE window that still opened (director-reported). Routing its toggle through -- ShowUIPanel is what subjects it to the same rules as everything else. UIPanelWindows["WorldMapFrame"] = { area = "full", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The cinematic letterbox (CinematicFrame.xml) — the ref's own line verbatim -- (UIParent.lua l.31). The row is what makes CINEMATIC_START's `ShowUIPanel(this, 1)` -- actually seat the frame: unregistered, ShowUIPanel takes its bare-`Show()` branch and -- the bars would appear without the panel manager ever closing what they cover. `full` -- because a fly-by owns the screen, and no `whileDead` — the ref gives it none, and a -- cinematic is not something a corpse needs. UIPanelWindows["CinematicFrame"] = { area = "full", pushable = 0 }
-- UIChildWindows — the ref's own table verbatim (UIParent.lua l.44-50; its comment: -- windows that "rely on a parent frame to be open. If the parent closes or a pushable -- frame overlaps them they must be hidden."). Dropped as "none exist yet" until 1507 — -- all four ship now: the open letter (MailFrame.xml) and the guild pane's three -- satellites (FriendsFrame.xml). The parent-close half is each parent's own OnHide -- (MailFrame hides the letter, FriendsFrame_OnHide hides the satellites); this table -- serves the OVERLAP half — SetCenterFrame's hide loop below — because the child popups -- sit exactly where the center seat puts a window. UIChildWindows = { "OpenMailFrame", "GuildControlPopupFrame", "GuildMemberDetailFrame", "GuildInfoFrame", }
-- The real client stores `.left`/`.center`/`.doublewide`/`.fullscreen` as fields directly on -- the `UIParent` frame table (UIParent.lua l.789-885). benilla has no `UIParent` frame object -- yet (a later decision's job) — so the two slots this v1 tracks live in a private chunk-local -- table instead of squatting the `UIParent` global name; a future `CreateFrame("Frame", -- "UIParent")` then lands cleanly on an empty global rather than silently coexisting with our -- state. Every function below is defined in this same chunk, so they all close over it. local slots = { left = nil, center = nil, fullscreen = nil, doublewide = nil }
-- SetLeftFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.809-824. Hides the old left occupant, SetPoints + -- Shows the new one at the left slot's screen anchor (verified: TOPLEFT UIParent, 0, -104). -- "UIParent" as the relativeTo name doesn't resolve to a real frame yet (none exists) — the -- engine's SetPoint falls back to the frame's own parent-or-screen default, which for our -- top-level panel frames IS the screen root, so this already anchors correctly; the string is -- kept for fidelity/forward-compat with the day a real UIParent frame lands. function SetLeftFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.left slots.left = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) — UIParent.lua l.826-850, the `UIChildWindows` hide -- loop (l.839-846) carried since 1507: a frame ARRIVING at the center seat lands exactly -- where the child popups sit, so they are put away first. Arriving is the ref's exact -- trigger — MovePanelToCenter's slide re-seats by direct assignment after a -- SetCenterFrame(nil), so a PUSHED panel does not run the loop; kept as transcribed. -- (The ref's `for index, value in UIChildWindows do` is Lua 5.0's iterator-less -- generic-for, which our VM cannot run — decision 1202; `ipairs` is the same walk.) function SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) local oldFrame = slots.center slots.center = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() if not skipSetPoint then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) end for _, name in ipairs(UIChildWindows) do local childWindow = getglobal(name) if childWindow then childWindow:Hide() end end end end
-- MovePanelToLeft() — UIParent.lua l.868-875: the center occupant slides back to the left slot -- (used when the left slot vacates and a "left-area" frame is holding center). function MovePanelToLeft() if slots.center then SetLeftFrame(nil) slots.center:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) slots.left = slots.center slots.center = nil end end
-- MovePanelToCenter() — UIParent.lua l.877-885: the left occupant slides to the center slot -- (used when a higher-`pushable` frame wants the left spot). `:Raise()` (l.881) has no benilla -- frame-level equivalent yet — guarded, same posture as the pin's `UnitIsDead` guard below. function MovePanelToCenter() if slots.left then SetCenterFrame(nil) slots.left:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) if slots.left.Raise then slots.left:Raise() end slots.center = slots.left slots.left = nil end end
-- GetLeftFrame / GetCenterFrame — UIParent.lua l.916-922. function GetLeftFrame() return slots.left end
function GetCenterFrame() return slots.center end
-- SetFullScreenFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.852-866, now complete. The reference hides -- the whole game UI behind the fullscreen frame by hiding `UIParent` itself, and shows it -- again when the slot empties. That line was dropped for years because hiding `UIParent` -- reached almost nothing: 72 `parent=` declarations were missing from the transcription, -- so the HUD was a forest of top-level frames with no edge to cascade along (decision -- 1734, which restored them). -- -- **`CinematicFrame` survives this on purpose.** The reference declares it with no parent -- at all — `<Frame name="CinematicFrame" setAllPoints="true" hidden="true" ...>` — which -- is exactly how the frame this function is *showing* escapes the hide it performs. Ours -- matches; do not give it one. function SetFullScreenFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.fullscreen slots.fullscreen = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then UIParent:Hide() frame:Show() else UIParent:Show() end end
function GetFullScreenFrame() return slots.fullscreen end
-- SetDoublewideFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.788-808. One frame takes the left AND center -- seats at once: both incumbents are dropped (nil'd first, then hidden — the order matters, -- since an OnHide that re-enters this manager must not find itself still seated), and the -- new frame lands at the left slot's own screen anchor, because a doublewide window simply -- starts where left starts and is wide enough to cover both. -- -- Note what the reference does NOT do: `HideUIPanel` has no doublewide branch (l.754-786), -- so nothing ever clears this seat — `UIParent.doublewide` keeps pointing at the auction -- window forever once it has been opened, and every later ShowUIPanel re-hides an -- already-hidden frame. We reproduce that rather than inventing a clear: `Hide()` on a -- hidden frame fires nothing, so the difference is unobservable, and a "fix" here would be -- a silent divergence in the one function every window's placement runs through. function SetDoublewideFrame(frame) local oldLeft = slots.left local oldCenter = slots.center slots.doublewide = frame slots.left = nil slots.center = nil if oldLeft then oldLeft:Hide() end if oldCenter then oldCenter:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- GetDoublewideFrame — UIParent.lua l.924-926. function GetDoublewideFrame() return slots.doublewide end
-- The area a frame is REGISTERED for — or nil, which is equally the answer for no frame at -- all and for a frame this manager has never heard of. Four rules below turn on exactly -- that question ("is a native-center window holding the screen?", "is the frame parked at -- center a left-area one that should slide back?"), and all four want an absent frame and -- an unregistered one to answer the same way. The reference open-codes the pair of nil -- checks at each site, which is four chances to leave one of them out. local function AreaOf(frame) local info = frame and UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] return info and info.area end
-- CanOpenPanels() — UIParent.lua l.887-910. Its dead-player arms are commented out in the -- reference itself (both of them, with the note that the fear/out-of-control gate was -- "previously"); what survives is one rule: **a native-center frame open ⇒ nothing else -- opens**. The game menu is the only such frame (decision 0674), so this reads: with the -- ESC menu up, no window opens — not from a keybind, not from an NPC's OPEN_WINDOW. function CanOpenPanels() if AreaOf(GetCenterFrame()) == "center" then return nil end return 1 end
-- IsOptionFrameOpen() — UIParent.lua l.996-1002, and the reference's own bag guard: it is -- the first line of `ToggleBag`, `ToggleBackpack` and `ToggleKeyRing`, so with an options -- window up a bag keybind does nothing at all. Distinct from CanOpenPanels above, which -- asks about the panel MANAGER's centre slot; this asks a fixed list of five frames by -- name, none of which is a managed panel. -- -- The reference checks GameMenuFrame, OptionsFrame, UIOptionsFrame, SoundOptionsFrame and -- KeyBindingFrame, and EVERY member is read through a nil guard here. That is the -- reference's own idiom, not a softening of it — it already writes -- `(KeyBindingFrame and KeyBindingFrame:IsVisible())` because that frame is created on -- demand — extended to the whole list, because "is an options screen up" has a correct -- answer, *no*, whenever the screen does not exist. -- -- Two of the five genuinely do not exist in this client: benilla folds the reference's -- three separate options windows into one `OptionsFrame` (its Video/Sound/Interface pages -- are tabs of it) and its key-bindings page is a page of that same window -- (KeyBindingsPage.xml), so `OptionsFrame` + `GameMenuFrame` cover every screen the other -- three name. Those two the manifest does guarantee — but a PARTIAL interface is a real -- surface (a focused test VM, and the reference's own `ADDON_LOADED` ordering), and this -- runs on the first line of every `ToggleBag`/`ToggleBackpack`/`ToggleKeyRing`, so it is -- the last place that should be the thing to raise. -- ── Moved here when UIDropDownMenu.xml went to the chain (1751) ────────────────────── -- The reference keeps `CloseMenus` in `UIParent.lua:984`, not in its dropdown file, and -- this file is already where our slice of UIParent.lua lives (`IsOptionFrameOpen` below, -- `CloseAllWindows`, `ToggleGameMenu`). It sits at manifest line 144, ahead of all five -- consumers — the stock dropdown at 155, MicroMenu, GameMenuFrame and two test kits. -- -- The BOUND is inlined rather than read from `UIDROPDOWNMENU_MAXLEVELS`, which lives in the -- dropdown file: a kit that loads this file and not that one would otherwise fail on -- `'for' limit must be a number`. Two is the reference's own list count (DropDownList1/2 are -- what `UIDropDownMenu.xml` declares; the third exists only in later builds). -- -- The BODY stays ours and is deliberately not the reference's: stock iterates a `UIMenus` -- table nothing here declares, ours asks the dropdown lists directly. Same answer, and it -- retires with this file rather than pretending to be stock. function CloseMenus() local closed for i=1, 2, 1 do local list = getglobal("DropDownList"..i) if list and list:IsVisible() then closed = 1 end end if closed then CloseDropDownMenus() end return closed end
function IsOptionFrameOpen() if (GameMenuFrame and GameMenuFrame:IsVisible()) or (OptionsFrame and OptionsFrame:IsVisible()) or (UIOptionsFrame and UIOptionsFrame:IsVisible()) or (SoundOptionsFrame and SoundOptionsFrame:IsVisible()) or (KeyBindingFrame and KeyBindingFrame:IsVisible()) then return 1 else return nil end end
-- Everything that can REFUSE an open, asked in the reference's own order (UIParent.lua -- l.663-689). Answers false when the frame must not open. Not a pure predicate, and that -- is the point: `force` is precisely the right to throw the incumbent out instead of being -- turned away, so each refusal and its eviction are one decision and are written as one. local function AdmitPanel(info, force) -- A dead player gets only the windows that asked for it (l.663-666) — and hears why: -- NotWhileDeadError is the binary's 0x48d340 (wow-re §5 cross-check, 2026-08-21 — -- decision 1507's open item): push id 0x7e into the message catalog, whose row is -- ERR_PLAYER_DEAD → UI_ERROR_MESSAGE, sound "NONE". Our binding (ui_errors.rs) -- pushes the same key onto the engine's client-local error queue, which the app -- resolves against GlobalStrings and fires as the same event. The binding is a pure -- display trigger — this line, like the reference's, decides WHEN. if UnitIsDead("player") and not info.whileDead then NotWhileDeadError() return false end -- l.668-675: nothing opens behind a full-screen frame. The world map is the only -- `full` row we register, so this reads: nothing opens behind the map. if GetFullScreenFrame() and info.area ~= "full" then if not force then return false end SetFullScreenFrame(nil) end -- l.677-689: with a native-center frame open, only another center request gets -- through. Redundant with the caller's CanOpenPanels gate for anything that doesn't -- force (the reference double-checks it too); kept because it is the ONLY path that -- can displace the menu, and dropping it would silently turn `force` into a no-op. -- No benilla caller passes `force` yet. if AreaOf(GetCenterFrame()) == "center" and info.area ~= "center" then if not force then return false end SetCenterFrame(nil) end return true end
-- Seating a **left-area** panel (l.719-751). The left slot is what it wants; `pushable` -- settles what happens to whoever is already sitting there. Read the comparisons as "the -- higher number is the one that gets moved along" — and two zeroes will not move for each -- other at all, which is what makes one NPC window replace another outright. local function SeatLeftAreaPanel(frame, info) local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() if not leftFrame then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end
local leftInfo = UIPanelWindows[leftFrame:GetName()] local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if centerFrame then -- Both seats taken (l.744-751): outrank the center occupant and it slides back to -- the left while we take center; otherwise settle for replacing the left one. if info.pushable > UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()].pushable then MovePanelToLeft() SetCenterFrame(frame) else SetLeftFrame(frame) end elseif leftInfo.pushable == 0 and info.pushable == 0 then -- Neither will budge — two NPC sessions — so we replace it outright (l.729-732, -- the gossip<->merchant case). SetLeftFrame(frame) elseif leftInfo.pushable > info.pushable then -- The incumbent outranks us, so it is promoted to center and we take the left slot -- it vacates (l.735-741 — highest priority goes to center). MovePanelToCenter() SetLeftFrame(frame) else SetCenterFrame(frame) end end
-- ShowUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.649-751, now the WHOLE slice: left, center, full -- and doublewide (pin §3 steps 1,3-5, plus the native-center mode decision 0674 needed and -- the `full` slot the world map took in 0203/0674). `doublewide` (l.706-716) arrived with -- the auction house, decision 1511 — the last arm below is now genuinely unreachable for a -- registered row and stays only as the defensive fallback its comment says it is. -- -- Two questions, in order: may it open at all, and where does it sit. function ShowUIPanel(frame, force) if not frame or frame:IsVisible() then return end
local info = UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] -- l.655-657. Note the reference's own precedence: an UNREGISTERED frame is not gated -- (the `info and` term), so a bare toplevel still shows with the menu up. The gate is -- asked unconditionally, because addons replace CanOpenPanels and expect to be asked. local panelsAllowed = CanOpenPanels() if not panelsAllowed and info and info.area ~= "center" then return end if not info then frame:Show() return end if not AdmitPanel(info, force) then return end

function UIFrameFadeIn(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) FadeToMode("IN", frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) end
function UIFrameFadeOut(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) FadeToMode("OUT", frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) end
function UIFrameFadeUpdate(elapsed) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do local frame = FADEFRAMES[index] local fadeInfo = frame.fadeInfo if not fadeInfo.fadeTimer then fadeInfo.fadeTimer = 0 end fadeInfo.fadeTimer = fadeInfo.fadeTimer + elapsed if fadeInfo.fadeTimer < fadeInfo.timeToFade then if fadeInfo.mode == "IN" then frame:SetAlpha((fadeInfo.fadeTimer / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.endAlpha - fadeInfo.startAlpha) + fadeInfo.startAlpha) elseif fadeInfo.mode == "OUT" then frame:SetAlpha(((fadeInfo.timeToFade - fadeInfo.fadeTimer) / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.startAlpha - fadeInfo.endAlpha) + fadeInfo.endAlpha) end else frame:SetAlpha(fadeInfo.endAlpha) if fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime and fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime > 0 then fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime = fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime - elapsed else UIFrameFadeRemoveFrame(frame) if fadeInfo.finishedFunc then fadeInfo.finishedFunc(fadeInfo.finishedArg1, fadeInfo.finishedArg2, fadeInfo.finishedArg3, fadeInfo.finishedArg4) fadeInfo.finishedFunc = nil end end end index = index + 1 end end
function UIFrameIsFading(frame) if FadeIndexOf(frame) then return 1 end return nil end
-- tDeleteItem(table, item) — ref UIParent.lua l.1376-1390, the reference's own array -- delete: it removes EVERY occurrence, closing the hole each time, and it is published -- surface (the pulse kit below is one caller; addons written against 1.12 are the rest). function tDeleteItem(t, item) local index = 1 while t[index] do if item == t[index] then table.remove(t, index) else index = index + 1 end end end
-- ── The button-pulse kit — ref UIParent.lua l.9 + l.1334-1373, transcribed ────────────── -- A button flashes its highlight on and off for a while: the reference uses it for the -- keyring button when the player picks up their first key (MainMenuBar.xml l.335), for the -- micro buttons on a new talent point (MainMenuBarMicroButtons.lua l.124) and for the -- tutorial frame's advance button (TutorialFrame.lua l.72). -- -- **Why it is here now.** Decision 0304 scoped pulses out while nothing called them. -- benilla now runs the reference's own `ContainerFrame.lua` off the player's chain (1751), -- and `ToggleKeyRing` closes with `SetButtonPulse(KeyRingButton, 0, 1)` — a *stop*, the -- duration-0 form — on every keyring open. A nil global there is a raise on a window the -- player is opening, and the honest fix is the reference's mechanism, not a guard at the -- call site: it is thirty lines and it makes the other three call sites work the day they -- arrive. -- -- Verbatim but for the tick source: the reference hangs ButtonPulse_OnUpdate on UIParent's -- OnUpdate (UIParent.xml l.16-22), which walks an empty list every frame forever. Ours is -- BenillaPulseDriver below — the same shape the fade kit already uses (and the same reason: -- the engine dispatches OnUpdate to visible frames only, so a driver that hides itself on -- an empty list costs nothing while idle, and SetButtonPulse, the single inserter, shows it -- again). PULSEBUTTONS = {}
function SetButtonPulse(button, duration, pulseRate) -- The reference really does write pulseDuration twice, the first time from pulseRate — -- its own comment on the next line ("pulseRate is actually seconds per pulse state") -- is why: pulseDuration counts down one HALF-cycle and is reloaded from pulseRate. button.pulseDuration = pulseRate button.pulseTimeLeft = duration button.pulseRate = pulseRate button.pulseOn = 0 tinsert(PULSEBUTTONS, button) BenillaPulseDriver:Show() end
function ButtonPulse_OnUpdate(elapsed) local index = 1 while PULSEBUTTONS[index] do local button = PULSEBUTTONS[index] if button.pulseTimeLeft > 0 then if button.pulseDuration < 0 then if button.pulseOn == 1 then button:UnlockHighlight() button.pulseOn = 0 else button:LockHighlight() button.pulseOn = 1 end button.pulseDuration = button.pulseRate end button.pulseDuration = button.pulseDuration - elapsed button.pulseTimeLeft = button.pulseTimeLeft - elapsed index = index + 1 else -- The duration-0 case, which is how `ToggleKeyRing` says "stop": the button is -- unhighlighted and dropped on the very first tick after the call. button:UnlockHighlight() button.pulseOn = 0 tDeleteItem(PULSEBUTTONS, button) -- No index bump — tDeleteItem closed the hole, so the next entry is here now. -- (The reference walks with `for index, button in PULSEBUTTONS` and deletes -- mid-walk, which skips the entry after each removal; this is the same walk -- FADEFRAMES already spells out longhand for the same reason.) end end end
function ButtonPulse_StopPulse(button) button:UnlockHighlight() button.pulseOn = 0 tDeleteItem(PULSEBUTTONS, button) end
-- The tab kit — `PanelTemplates_*` — is the REFERENCE's, off the player's chain -- (`Interface\FrameXML\UIPanelTemplates.lua`, seated below this file in the manifest). -- Our eleven transcribed copies stood here dead from the day that entry landed, and one -- of them was carrying a benilla-only return the settle below read (1855/1860). What -- stays is that settle, which is ours because our text measure is a frame late and the -- reference's is not.
-- The tab template's per-frame settle: the ref does TabResize(0) once, in OnShow -- (CharacterFrameTemplates.xml l.77-80), trusting a synchronous text measure. Our -- GetStringWidth has a frame of latency, so the template's OnUpdate calls this until the -- measured width settles (then it's a no-op compare per frame). The ref sizes the hover -- highlight alongside it; this kit does not — both tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own side edges, so it is the tab by construction and no settle can desync it -- (decision 1004). -- -- The fit PARAMETERS live on the tab (`benillaTabPadding`/`benillaTabMaxWidth`, defaulting -- to the +0 fit every window tab has always used) rather than at the call site, because -- there is exactly one call site and it is this settle loop: an instance that ran its own -- TabResize in OnLoad — as the reference's macro tabs do — would just be overwritten on the -- next frame. Setting the two fields IS how an instance asks for the reference's own fit. -- THE STRUCTURAL CLAMP — a tab may never grow past its window's drawn right edge, whatever -- the instance asked for (decision 1002; the director's "fix this properly to prevent it -- ever again"). The reference's own caps are numbers hand-tuned to ITS font: the macro -- window's 150 is right for the enUS FRIZQT__ the 1.12 client rasterizes and for nothing -- else in particular, and the label it guards carries a CHARACTER NAME — the one string -- whose width no window author can know. So the instance's cap is a preference and the -- window's edge is the law. -- -- `benillaTabRightInset` is how a window declares how far its DRAWN plate stops short of -- its frame rect, because no kit can introspect an art margin. The macro window's is 40: -- its 384-unit frame is painted by a 256-wide slice plus a 128-wide one that carries a -- transparent tail. Clamping to the frame rect instead — the first attempt — clamped to a -- boundary the player cannot see, and the tab still walked out over the world. -- -- The clamp is applied to the RESULT, through TabResize's own `absoluteSize` arm, rather -- than folded into `maxWidth`: that parameter is compared against `text + padding` but -- assigned as `maxWidth + padding`, so a room budget expressed through it is off by the -- padding and silently fails to bind. `absoluteSize` sets the tab width outright, which is -- exactly what a room budget is. function BenillaTab_Room(tab) local parent = tab:GetParent() if not parent then return nil end local left, right = tab:GetLeft(), parent:GetRight() if not left or not right then return nil end local room = (right - (tab.benillaTabRightInset or 0)) - left if room < 1 then room = 1 end return room end
function BenillaTabButton_OnUpdate(tab) local name = tab:GetName() local text = getglobal(name .. "Text") local w = (text and text:GetStringWidth()) or 0 if w <= 0 then return end local pad = tab.benillaTabPadding or 0 local room = BenillaTab_Room(tab) if tab.benillaFitWidth == w and tab.benillaFitRoom == room then return end tab.benillaFitWidth, tab.benillaFitRoom = w, room PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, nil, tab.benillaTabMaxWidth) -- THE CLAMP READS THE FIT BACK OFF THE ART, not off a return value and not off the -- button. `PanelTemplates_TabResize` is the REFERENCE's now (1837 put -- `UIPanelTemplates.lua` on the chain below this file, so its definition wins) and it -- returns nothing; our own copy's benilla-only `return tabWidth` had already stopped -- running, which is what took 1002's clamp off the air silently. `tab:GetWidth()` -- cannot serve either — it reads the last RESOLVED rect, this frame's stale input -- inside a settle, which is the whole reason 1002 added that return. -- -- `$parentMiddle` can. `PanelTemplates_TabResize` sets it on its way out, a Texture's -- width is its AUTHORED size, and a region's GetWidth reports the authored value -- without consulting a resolved rect (region::virtual_span) — so it is the number the -- verb just computed, same tick. The tab is that plus its two end caps, which is the -- reference's own `tabWidth = width + sideWidths`. if room then local middle = getglobal(name .. "Middle") local left = getglobal(name .. "Left") local fitted = (middle and middle:GetWidth() or 0) + 2 * (left and left:GetWidth() or 0) if fitted > room then PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, room) end end -- No highlight sizing here on purpose — BOTH tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own two side edges, so it IS the tab by construction (decision 1004). end
